title: CameraRig
description: Parsed shape of a character's camera.json asset (3D characters only). Rigs a camera per emote for the 3D viewport, which — unlike a 2D sprite — has no framing baked into the art. Poses are normalized to the character's height so a rig is stable across models and scales. A `default` resting shot applies everywhere; each emote may override it. See assets/README.md for authoring and playback semantics.

default.description: Resting shot applied to every emote's idle/talking loop unless the emote overrides it. Usually a static Pose.

emotes.description: Per-emote camera, keyed by the emote's `key` (the char.ini [emote <name>] block name).

Pose.description: A camera framing, normalized to character height. Every field is an override of the resolved default, so a partial pose (e.g. only `distance`) inherits the rest. A bare Pose used as a Clip is a static hold.

targetY.description: Height the camera looks at, as a fraction of the character's height (0 = feet, 1 = head).

distance.description: Camera distance from the target, in character-heights.

yaw.description: Horizontal orbit in degrees; 0 = facing the character head-on, positive = orbit to the character's left.

pitch.description: Vertical orbit in degrees; 0 = level, positive = looking down.

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees.

Keyframe.description: A Pose at a point in time. `t` is normalized 0..1 across the phase's driving motion (the preanim VMD for a preanim clip, the base loop for a loop clip), so keys retime automatically if the motion length changes.

KeyedClip.description: An animated camera: poses interpolated over the phase. A loop clip's first and last keys should match (t=0 and t=1) so the cycle is seamless.

Clip.description: Either a static Pose (a bare framing object) or an animated KeyedClip (has a `keys` array). The two are disjoint: a Pose has no `keys`.

EmoteCamera.description: Camera for one emote. `loop` is the idle/talking shot (static or looping); `preanim` is a one-shot played during the preanim phase, after which the camera eases back to `loop`. Both optional: absent `loop` falls back to the rig `default`; absent `preanim` means the preanim phase keeps the loop shot.
